headline: Castione trail run banked — strong finish, race long behind us now
summary: Today's session was a 2h58 trail run at Castione (19.6km, 1188m D+, up to 1995m) with HR mostly 141-155bpm per the lap summary, average 143bpm — comfortably aerobic despite the climbing. RPE 8 but feel was 1 (Strong), which is a good combination: hard work, body responding well. No pain or ITB mentions logged. This lands two days after the Valtellina Wine Trail race itself (Nov 7), so we're now into post-race rebuild territory rather than taper — CTL sits at 54.8, ATL 54.4, ramp -1.3/wk, which is calm. HRV 51 and RHR 49 this morning are unremarkable given yesterday's reading was similar (HRV 48/RHR 49), and sleep was short again (5h15, score 60) — worth watching but not a red flag on a day you've already banked a solid altitude session on.
flags: Three of the last four nights have been under 6h sleep (5h19, 5h48, 5h15) with sleep scores sliding 79→60 — a mild fatigue-debt pattern worth flagging even though today's session went well.
Session is at ~1450-1995m average/max altitude: treat today's resting HR/HRV as noise-prone from altitude, not a fatigue signal in isolation.
suggestedChange: Given short sleep three nights running post-race, consider an easier or shorter session tomorrow to let sleep debt clear before building rebuild volume back up — confirm with Alberto rather than assuming.
